Create one original fine-art surreal photograph, portrait 4:5 composition, a quiet physically tactile image rather than an illustration or an advertisement. We stand in the shadow of a modest old seaside apartment doorway looking onto a narrow weathered balcony just before sunrise. One large washed indigo cotton bedsheet is suspended by three mismatched wooden clothes pegs on a taut line. In the upper half it is unmistakably ordinary heavy wet cotton with weave, small mends, irregular folds and a stitched hem; as the breeze lifts its lower half toward the viewer, the cloth gradually becomes a shallow rolling sheet of real seawater, its folding ridge turning into a tiny white breaking wave, still visibly continuous with the cloth rather than a picture printed on it. The lifted lower edge curls diagonally across the frame, a few droplets hanging beneath it. Salt-white stitches echo the delicate broken foam. The water is held up softly like fabric, not pouring as a waterfall. A shallow wet crescent on the old terracotta floor reflects dim blue light, with one worn ordinary pale slipper outside it. Nothing miniature. No people. Beyond the dark iron railing, only a pale hazy sliver of actual sea and horizon, kept subdued. Restrained mineral colors: indigo, cool pearl-grey dawn, oxidized umber floor, tiny natural wood warmth; no golden sunlight. Composition intimate and asymmetrical, sheet occupies two thirds, dark doorframe on the left, enough stillness around it to breathe. Side-lit moist cotton fibers and fine suspended spray. Believable lens perspective, subtle medium-format film grain, imperfect inhabited materials, soft natural light, one seamless impossible material transition. Emotional atmosphere comes from touch and silence, not symbols. No writing, no typography, no quote, no logos, no miniature city, no pedestal, no glossy CGI, no decorative flowers, no spectacle, no excessive props.
